questions.question: How do you retry a failed operation in Ruby?
questions.title: The Retry Pattern
questions.direct_answer: retry (inside a rescue) re-runs the begin block from the top, used to retry a transient failure (a flaky network call). You must guard it with a counter so you don't retry forever: attempt = 0; begin; attempt += 1; api.call; rescue NetworkError => e; raise if attempt >= 3; sleep(2 ** attempt); retry; end. This retries up to N times with exponential backoff (sleep 1, 2, 4...) before giving up and re-raising. retry is for transient, recoverable errors only; don't retry a bug (it'll fail the same way forever). The gem 'retryable' wraps this, but the hand-rolled version shows you understand backoff.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know retry re-runs the begin block, must be guarded by a counter, and uses backoff; and that it's for transient errors only.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Unguarded retry (infinite loop) or retrying a deterministic bug (it fails the same way forever).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: retry re-runs the begin block; guard with a counter + backoff; re-raise after N tries. For transient failures only, not bugs.

sections.title: Retry With a Counter and Backoff
sections.content: retry, inside a rescue, re-runs the begin block from the top, used to retry a transient failure like a flaky network call. You must guard it with a counter so you don't retry forever: set attempt to zero, begin, increment attempt, call the API, rescue NetworkError, raise if attempt is at least three, sleep with exponential backoff, and retry. This retries up to N times with exponential backoff — sleep 1, then 2, then 4 — before giving up and re-raising. retry is for transient, recoverable errors only; don't retry a bug because it'll fail the same way forever and you'll loop until the process dies. The gem retryable wraps this, but the hand-rolled version shows you understand backoff.

sections.title: rescue -> sleep -> retry
sections.content:
On a transient error, back off and retry; re-raise after N tries.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  B[begin: attempt+=1; call] -->|ok| D[done]
  B -->|raise| R[rescue]
  R -->|attempt < max| S[sleep backoff] --> B
  R -->|attempt >= max| X[re-raise]
```

sections.title: Retry with backoff
sections.content:
```ruby
def call_with_retry(api, max_attempts: 3)
  attempt = 0
  begin
    attempt += 1
    api.call                       # may raise NetworkError
  rescue NetworkError => e
    raise if attempt >= max_attempts   # give up after N tries
    sleep(2 ** (attempt - 1))           # 1s, 2s, 4s (exponential backoff)
    retry                              # re-run the begin block
  end
end

# Use it for TRANSIENT failures only:
#   - network timeouts
#   - rate-limited (429) API
#   - a brief infra blip
# DON'T retry a bug (ArgumentError) — it fails the same way every time.

# The 'retryable' gem wraps this, but the hand-rolled version shows backoff.
```

sections.title: Retry Rules
rows: bugs fail the same way forever

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Unguarded retry — it loops forever on a persistent failure.
Retrying a deterministic bug (ArgumentError) — it fails the same way every time.
No backoff (sleep) — hammering the server makes the failure worse.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: retry (inside a rescue) re-runs the begin block from the top.
ALWAYS guard it with a counter and re-raise after N tries (avoid infinite loops).
Add exponential backoff (sleep 1, 2, 4...) between retries to ease the server.
retry is for TRANSIENT failures (network, rate-limit) — not for bugs.
Don't retry a deterministic error (ArgumentError) — it fails identically forever.
